correctness.rationale: The observed-set partition gives J_n exactly; algebra yields Delta_1=2(pq)^2 and Delta_2=pq[-2(pq)^2+7pq-1]. For moderate dominance both terms of the general difference are positive. For larger dominance, after division by positive qp^n the increment H_n is strictly increasing: its difference has two leading terms with positive sum by ((1+p)p^4-(2p-1))=(p^2+p-1)(p^3+p-1)>0, and a third strictly positive term. H_n tends to 1, establishing the unique trough sign phase. The asymptotic 1/4 excursion is established by p^n approaching 1/2. Continuity yields strict finite sign patterns in all positive richness dimensions. The exact standard-library checker replays 512 checks; finite checks are not substitutes for the analytic proof.

value.rationale: Jaccard autosimilarity between surveys of the same assemblage is a standard ecological proxy for sample representativeness and effort standardization. This exact phase law identifies when expected similarity is noninjective and counter-monotone in sampling effort, with a closed abundance threshold, a uniqueness theorem for the trough, an almost 25-percentage-point excursion, and strictly positive arbitrary-richness realizations. Such a mathematical boundary informs interpretation and choice of sampling effort; it is not merely a renaming or one-off numerical counterexample.
